```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Toft renders this once, at build time, with `rmarkdown::render` into
# toft-render/, and serves the directory that falls out. There is no R
# process behind the page a viewer loads, so nothing here can be interactive and
# nothing here should try: what the reader gets is exactly what this render saw.
#
# The render runs with the app's environment variables, which is the edge worth
# knowing about. It is what lets this report read REPORT_DATA below; it is also
# why a report that reads a connection string and prints it has published that
# connection string to everyone who can read the page.
#
# One .Rmd at the repository root, and that is a requirement rather than a
# style: the root's .Rmd files are what Toft counts to decide which
# document is the app, and two of them is ambiguous. Helpers belong in a
# subdirectory, which is where data/make-sample.R lives.

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8.5, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 110)

env <- function(name, fallback) {
  value <- trimws(Sys.getenv(name, ""))
  if (nzchar(value)) value else fallback
}

data_file <- env("REPORT_DATA", "data/deliveries.csv")
max_rows <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(env("REPORT_MAX_ROWS", "200000")))
if (is.na(max_rows) || max_rows < 1) max_rows <- 200000L

# A missing file is a first-class outcome, not a crash. A build that dies with
# "cannot open file" makes somebody read a build log to discover that a nightly
# export did not land; a report that says so on its own front page does not.
readable <- file.exists(data_file)
if (readable) {
  raw <- utils::read.csv(data_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                         na.strings = c("", "NA", "null"), nrows = max_rows)
  truncated <- nrow(raw) == max_rows
} else {
  raw <- data.frame()
  truncated <- FALSE
}

key_column <- {
  declared <- trimws(Sys.getenv("REPORT_KEY", ""))
  if (nzchar(declared) && declared %in% names(raw)) declared
  else if (ncol(raw) > 0) names(raw)[1]
  else NA_character_
}

numeric_cols <- names(raw)[vapply(raw, is.numeric, logical(1))]
text_cols <- setdiff(names(raw), numeric_cols)

pct <- function(x, total) {
  if (total == 0) return("--")
  paste0(formatC(100 * x / total, format = "f", digits = 1), "%")
}
big <- function(x) formatC(as.integer(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
num <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_character_)
  formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 4)
}

# One table style for the whole document. kable ships with knitr, which
# rmarkdown already requires, so this costs no dependency.
show <- function(df, caption = NULL) {
  knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
               table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"')
}

frame <- function(mar = c(4, 4.5, 1.2, 1)) {
  par(mar = mar, bg = "white", las = 1, cex.axis = 0.9,
      col.axis = "#5A5F6B", col.lab = "#5A5F6B", fg = "#E5E6EA", family = "sans")
}

# The house palette, so a base-R plot matches every other example in the
# gallery. `--lp-c1` and `--lp-dan-solid` from toft-kit.css.
bar_fill  <- "#4338CA"
flag_fill <- "#EF4444"

# Emit raw HTML from an `asis` chunk.
#
# The indentation below is for whoever reads this file; pandoc reads a line
# indented four spaces as a code block, which is how a masthead ends up on the
# page as source. So it is stripped on the way out.
html_block <- function(x) {
  cat("\n```{=html}\n")
  cat(gsub("(?m)^[ \\t]+", "", x, perl = TRUE))
  cat("\n```\n\n")
}
```

```{r masthead, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cap <- function(label, on, note = "") sprintf(
  '<span class="cap %s" title="%s"><b>%s</b></span>',
  if (isTRUE(on)) "on" else "off", note, label)

on_platform <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("TOFT_APP_TOKEN"))

html_block(sprintf('
<div class="lp-block">
  <div class="masthead"><div class="masthead-in">
    <div>
      <div class="wordmark"><span class="mark"></span>
        <span class="wordmark-text">Toft example</span></div>
      <h1>%s</h1>
      <p class="standfirst">Point it at a CSV and it says what is wrong with the file.
         Seven checks, rendered once at deploy time and served as the document that
         fell out.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="masthead-aside">
      <span class="chip chip-lang">R &middot; R Markdown</span>
      <span class="chip">%s</span>
    </div>
  </div></div>
  <div class="rail"><div class="rail-in">
    <span class="rail-label">Toft</span>%s
  </div></div>
</div>',
  if (nzchar(trimws(Sys.getenv("REPORT_TITLE", "")))) Sys.getenv("REPORT_TITLE")
  else "Data Quality Report",
  format(Sys.time(), "%d %B %Y at %H:%M %Z"),
  paste0(
    cap("R Markdown", TRUE,
        "An .Rmd at the release root, rendered once at build time with rmarkdown::render into toft-render/ and served as a document."),
    cap("Built at deploy", TRUE,
        "Nothing is re-rendered by a restart. Only a deploy produces a new document \u2014 and a schedule on the app\u2019s Overview tab makes that deploy happen on a cron expression."),
    cap("The data", readable,
        if (readable) data_file else paste(data_file, "is not there \u2014 which this report says on its own front page rather than failing the build")),
    cap("renv.lock", file.exists("renv.lock"),
        "Committed, so the Dependencies tab can enumerate this app. Without one nothing is installed and the app fails at its first library() call."),
    cap("No network", TRUE,
        "Nothing here contacts anything. Everything below is derived from one file."),
    cap("Toft workload", on_platform,
        if (on_platform) "Rendered as a Toft workload." else "Rendered outside Toft."),
    collapse = "")))
```

```{r missing-file, eval = !readable, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf(
"## The data is not there yet\n\nThis report expected to read `%s`, relative to the release directory, and no such file exists.\n\nThat is normal for a while on a fresh install: something else — a nightly export, a scheduled job, a person with a volume browser — puts the file there. Point `REPORT_DATA` at it, or deploy again once it has landed. **A render is a deploy**, so nothing here re-reads the file on its own.\n",
data_file))
```

```{r overview, eval = readable, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf(
"## What was profiled\n\n`%s` — **%s rows**, **%d columns**, read at build time.%s\n\nEverything below is derived from that file alone. Nothing is written back to it, and nothing here contacts a network.\n",
data_file, big(nrow(raw)), ncol(raw),
if (truncated) sprintf(" The read stopped at the `REPORT_MAX_ROWS` limit of %s, so this is a profile of the first %s rows and not of the whole file.", big(max_rows), big(max_rows)) else ""))
```

```{r column-profile, eval = readable, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## Every column at a glance\n\nThe first thing to read. A column that is 40% empty, or that holds one distinct value across the whole file, is usually a pipeline fault rather than a fact about the world.\n\n")

profile <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(raw), function(nm) {
  col <- raw[[nm]]
  missing <- sum(is.na(col))
  data.frame(
    Column = nm,
    Type = if (is.numeric(col)) "numeric" else if (is.logical(col)) "logical" else "text",
    Missing = sprintf("%s (%s)", big(missing), pct(missing, nrow(raw))),
    Distinct = big(length(unique(col[!is.na(col)]))),
    Smallest = if (is.numeric(col)) num(suppressWarnings(min(col, na.rm = TRUE))) else
      { v <- sort(unique(as.character(col[!is.na(col)]))); if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_character_ },
    Largest = if (is.numeric(col)) num(suppressWarnings(max(col, na.rm = TRUE))) else
      { v <- sort(unique(as.character(col[!is.na(col)]))); if (length(v)) v[length(v)] else NA_character_ },
    Mean = if (is.numeric(col)) num(mean(col, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_character_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
print(show(profile))
```

```{r missingness, eval = readable && nrow(raw) > 0, results = "asis", fig.height = 3.6}
missing_counts <- vapply(raw, function(c) sum(is.na(c)), integer(1))
cat(sprintf("\n## Missing values\n\n%s of %s rows are complete across every column.\n\n",
            big(sum(stats::complete.cases(raw))), big(nrow(raw))))
if (any(missing_counts > 0)) {
  ord <- order(missing_counts, decreasing = TRUE)
  ord <- ord[missing_counts[ord] > 0]
  frame(mar = c(4, 9, 1.2, 1))
  bp <- barplot(rev(100 * missing_counts[ord] / nrow(raw)), horiz = TRUE,
                names.arg = rev(names(missing_counts)[ord]), col = bar_fill,
                border = NA, xlab = "Missing (% of rows)", cex.names = 0.9)
  text(rev(100 * missing_counts[ord] / nrow(raw)), bp,
       labels = rev(big(missing_counts[ord])), pos = 4, cex = 0.8, xpd = NA)
} else {
  cat("No column has a missing value.\n")
}
```

```{r duplicates, eval = readable && !is.na(key_column), results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf("\n## Duplicate keys\n\n`%s` is treated as the key column — the first column, unless `REPORT_KEY` names another.\n\n",
            key_column))
keys <- as.character(raw[[key_column]])
counts <- table(keys[!is.na(keys)])
repeated <- counts[counts > 1]
if (length(repeated) == 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Every one of the %s values is unique.\n", big(length(counts))))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("**%s value%s appear%s more than once**, accounting for %s extra row%s. A key that repeats usually means an export ran twice.\n\n",
              big(length(repeated)), if (length(repeated) == 1) "" else "s",
              if (length(repeated) == 1) "s" else "",
              big(sum(repeated) - length(repeated)),
              if (sum(repeated) - length(repeated) == 1) "" else "s"))
  top <- sort(repeated, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(10, length(repeated)))]
  print(show(data.frame(Value = names(top), Rows = as.integer(top), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
}
```

```{r categories, eval = readable && length(text_cols) > 0, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## Categories that are the same thing spelled differently\n\nCase and stray whitespace are the quiet ones: `North`, `north` and ` North` group as three regions in every tool that has ever read this file, and nothing warns you.\n\n")

collisions <- do.call(rbind, lapply(text_cols, function(nm) {
  values <- as.character(raw[[nm]])
  values <- values[!is.na(values)]
  if (!length(values)) return(NULL)
  distinct <- unique(values)
  # Too many distinct values means this is free text or an identifier, not a
  # category, and every pair of near-matches in it would be noise.
  if (length(distinct) > 50) return(NULL)
  normalised <- tolower(trimws(distinct))
  grouped <- split(distinct, normalised)
  grouped <- grouped[vapply(grouped, length, integer(1)) > 1]
  if (!length(grouped)) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(grouped), function(g) {
    variants <- grouped[[g]]
    data.frame(Column = nm,
               `Reads as` = g,
               `Spelled` = paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", encodeString(variants, quote = '"'),
                                         vapply(variants, function(v) big(sum(values == v)), character(1))),
                                 collapse = ", "),
               check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))

if (is.null(collisions)) {
  cat("No column has two spellings of one value.\n")
} else {
  print(show(collisions))
}
```

```{r outliers, eval = readable && length(numeric_cols) > 0, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## Numbers that do not belong\n\nTukey's rule — more than one and a half interquartile ranges outside the quartiles — which is exactly what a boxplot draws as dots. It flags honest extremes as well as broken ones, so it is a list to read rather than a verdict.\n\n")

flags <- do.call(rbind, lapply(numeric_cols, function(nm) {
  col <- raw[[nm]][!is.na(raw[[nm]])]
  if (length(col) < 4) return(NULL)
  q <- stats::quantile(col, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE)
  iqr <- q[2] - q[1]
  if (iqr == 0) return(NULL)
  low <- q[1] - 1.5 * iqr
  high <- q[2] + 1.5 * iqr
  out <- col[col < low | col > high]
  nonpositive <- sum(col <= 0)
  if (!length(out) && nonpositive == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    Column = nm,
    `Outside` = sprintf("%s to %s", num(low), num(high)),
    `Outliers` = sprintf("%s (%s)", big(length(out)), pct(length(out), length(col))),
    `Largest seen` = if (length(out)) num(out[which.max(abs(out - stats::median(col)))]) else "",
    `Zero or negative` = big(nonpositive),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

if (is.null(flags)) {
  cat("No numeric column has a value outside Tukey's fences.\n")
} else {
  print(show(flags))
  cat("\nA **zero or negative** count is worth a second look on its own: a duration, a weight or a price that is not positive is usually a clock, a unit or a decimal point rather than an unusual delivery.\n")
}
```

```{r distributions, eval = readable && length(numeric_cols) > 0, fig.height = 3.4, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## Distributions\n\nOne histogram per numeric column, on its own scale. The dashed line is the median; a distribution whose mean sits far from it is being pulled by the values in the table above.\n\n")
for (nm in numeric_cols) {
  col <- raw[[nm]][!is.na(raw[[nm]])]
  if (length(col) < 2 || length(unique(col)) < 2) next
  frame()
  hist(col, breaks = "Sturges", col = bar_fill, border = "white",
       main = "", xlab = nm)
  abline(v = stats::median(col), col = flag_fill, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  title(main = nm, adj = 0, cex.main = 1, font.main = 1)
}
```

```{r checks, eval = readable, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## What this report checks\n\n")
checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c("Shape", "Missing values", "Duplicate keys", "Category spelling",
            "Outliers", "Non-positive numbers", "Distributions"),
  `What it looks for` = c(
    "Row and column counts, and whether the read hit its row limit.",
    "Per column and per row, so a column that is mostly empty is visible next to a file that is mostly complete.",
    "Values of the key column appearing on more than one row.",
    "Values in a low-cardinality column that differ only by case or surrounding whitespace.",
    "Values beyond 1.5 interquartile ranges from the quartiles.",
    "Zeros and negatives in numeric columns, counted separately from outliers.",
    "The shape of each numeric column, with its median marked."),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(show(checks))
cat("\nNothing here is specific to the sample file. Point `REPORT_DATA` at any CSV and the same seven checks run against its columns.\n")
```
